title: Mineral nutrition and deficiency diagnosis — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define an evidence-led cannabis nutrition and deficiency-diagnosis SOP foundation without converting bounded nutrient-response studies into universal feed recipes.

excludedUntilValidated: universal EC or ppm feeding chart
automatic correction from a single tissue or solution result
direct transfer of one hydroponic study's optimum concentrations to other cultivars, stages or media

claims.statement: Single-element deficiencies in cannabis can produce recognizable foliar and growth patterns, but symptom onset and tissue nutrient concentration do not always correspond cleanly, so diagnosis should integrate multiple evidence types.
claims.boundary: Controlled single-element omission symptoms do not prove that a visually similar facility problem has the same cause.

claims.statement: Cannabis nutrient deficiencies can materially reduce vegetative growth and inflorescence yield, making timely detection and evidence-based correction operationally important.
claims.boundary: Magnitude of loss varies by element, severity, duration, genotype, stage and production system.

claims.statement: Nutrient diagnosis should separate direct observations from hypotheses and review root-zone pH/EC, irrigation/water status, source-water chemistry, formulation history, crop stage and root condition before concluding that a symptom is a primary nutrient deficiency.
claims.boundary: Visual symptomology alone cannot distinguish every deficiency, toxicity, uptake limitation, root disorder or environmental look-alike.

claims.statement: Cannabis N, P and K responses are interactive rather than independent, and vegetative-stage growth responses can change as combinations of supplied nutrients change.
claims.boundary: Response-surface optima are experimental outcomes for defined conditions, not universal nutrient-solution specifications.

claims.statement: Flowering-stage cannabis yield responses to nitrogen and phosphorus can be nonlinear, demonstrating that more fertilizer does not automatically produce more yield or quality.
claims.boundary: The tested deep-water-culture ranges and cultivar do not establish general flowering feed targets for other systems.

claims.statement: Vegetative and flowering cannabis studies support treating crop stage as a controlled context for nutrient interpretation rather than carrying one nutrient target unchanged through the entire lifecycle.
claims.boundary: Stage-specific evidence remains genotype- and system-dependent and should be validated before facility adoption.

claims.statement: Tissue analysis is most useful when sample location, crop stage, symptom status, method and corresponding root-zone or solution context are preserved so results can be compared meaningfully.
claims.boundary: A laboratory concentration without sampling context does not automatically identify root cause or authorize a recipe change.

claims.statement: Corrective nutrition actions should be verified with follow-up plant observations and compatible root-zone, solution or tissue measurements rather than closed solely because a feed adjustment was made.
claims.boundary: Process correction does not prove recovery until crop and measurement evidence support it.

releaseGates: chemical/fertilizer label and safety review where applicable
